author: SSJObscurity
quote: Recently replayed OoT, MM and WW. Age has definitely shown in these games. That aside, for their time, these are all fantastic games. Original music that just makes the world feel absolutely magical. Great journeys that allow you to feel like the true hero. These games feel just like they did when I was a kid and played them. Because they have aged and obviously you can tell because of aged gameplay mechanics and graphics, I will not let age affect my review because this game was still so much fun. The remake was announced and I wanted to re experience them before it came out to be able to compare it. Such a beautiful story  , a journey, that had passion and love poured into it. A good game like this is truly rare to come by, even when it is aged like this and you still enjoy it. I have truly been **** back into my childhood and am only finding myself having fun replaying other old Legend of Zelda titles over most other games releasing today. For the last several months, I have barely touched any other game. These games are timeless when it comes to the true beauty and experiences. The new remake only shows that. With some graphical improvements on a newer engine and improved gameplay mechanics, even a 28 year old game can still be the magical property it always was. The formula worked then, and it holds up even now.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998)

author: SSJObscurity
quote: 13 years… $2 billion. Where did it all go? Rockstar starved their player base for 13 years and over hyped their game so much and they didn’t even realize they were releasing an unfinished product. The game is in an abysmal state. Even in a ps5 pro you absolutely DO NOT get a steady 30 fps. A new generation game on a new generation console and it’s still locked at 30 fps. GTA 5 was at 30 fps. Rockstar has made yet another terrible decision 13 years later by refusing to make the game for pc along side of console and allowing players to just play it on the more powerful system that they want to play it on. Where did that $2 billion go? Into their wallets? Like how can critics rate this a perfect 100 in the state that it’s in? This is why you should never trust reviews. Also, once again, rockstar has opted to not release online on day one. Online is literally gta. The story for gta 6 was no where near as good as 5 or 4. The game had improved gameplay mechanics and graphics, when you aren’t worrying about horrendous frame drops. Several sequences of the game were so boring I almost didn’t continue playing. I feel asleep a few hours into borderlands 4 and never played again, this was almost a close second. I will give credit where it’s due, there are several other sections that are fun. The game feels like it plays like the old games with improved visuals though. It’s dated. The driving was slow like molasses at some points and wonky. The gunplay was horrible. Gta has always had bad gunplay and they still have yet to improve it. Making me question how reviewers could say this is a 100. This release was as rocky as cyberpunk and should receive the same treatment that cyberpunk did. So to be fair, and to be unbiased, which I have always loved playing gta online with friends and the story solo, but this game at its current state, does not deserve to be rated any higher than cyberpunk was on release. In the future, when they release it in pc and have the bugs fixed, this game will be a very fun game. Wait until then.

author: SSJObscurity
quote: Nintendo knows how to do a remake justice. Faithfully keeps the original experience and formula of the game while also delivering a smoother and much more enjoyable quality experience simultaneously. Improved graphics in a new engine with improved gameplay mechanics allow for you to experience the same nostalgic game that you remember but also allowing new players to the game to experience it with the improved gameplay experience. Feels just like being a kid again and playing it for the first time.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
